sections.title: 一、詞彙與慣用語(15%)
sections.instructions: 說明︰第1至15題，每題選出最適當的一個選項，標示在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。每題答對得1分，答錯不倒扣。

sections.title: 三、綜合測驗(10%)
sections.instructions: 說明︰第21至30題，每題一個空格，請依文意選出最適當的一個選項，標示在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。每題答對得1分，答錯不倒扣。

groups.passage:
Now that you are planning to go to college, how can you select an ideal college for yourself? [[21]] its reputation or the test scores it requires for admission? In fact, it is not [[22]] simple as that. College education is far more complicated than [[23]] the reputation of a college or the test scores it requires. In addition to these two factors, you should also have [[24]] important information. Finding out which college suits you involves time and energy, but [[25]] more than those you might spend on buying a motorcycle or a computer.
Here are some tips [[26]] choosing an ideal one from a number of colleges.
1. Visit the websites of these colleges and find out which college has departments [[27]] courses that interest you or will help you prepare for your future career.
2. Are the professors in the departments you plan to [[28]] into experts in their own fields?
3. Do the colleges allow you to participate in activities [[29]] will help you develop yourself intellectually and emotionally?
I hope the [[30]] advice is helpful to you in selecting the right college.

sections.title: 四、文意選填(10%)
sections.instructions: 說明：第31至40題，每題一個空格，請依文意在文章後所提供的 (A) 到 (J) 選項中分別選出最適當者，並將其英文字母代號標示在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。每題答對得1分，答錯不倒扣。

groups.passage: Can young people really improve the world by influencing their elders to change a policy? Read this story and decide for [[31]]. Dolphins, like most of us, love to eat tuna. So in many parts of the world dolphins and fishermen are in [[32]] for tuna. In the past, there wasn’t much conflict [[33]] dolphins and fishermen, because the numbers of tuna in the ocean were enormous. Now, however, men have developed huge fishing nets that form underwater “walls” that [[34]] for miles. They can catch thousands of tuna at one time. Unfortunately, they [[35]] catch many dolphins at the same time. Dolphins, like us, have to breathe air. When they are [[36]] in the nets too long, they cannot breathe. By the time they are brought [[37]] the ship, they will be dead. Many children were upset to hear about the [[38]] death of these wonderful sea creatures and decided to help [[39]] them. They wrote letters to the tuna companies and supermarkets asking them to find a way to spare dolphins. Eventually their hard work paid [[40]]. Now you can buy tuna with the label “dolphin-free tuna.” So you see, everyone can make a difference.

sections.title: 五、閱讀測驗(30%)
sections.instructions: 說明︰第41至55題，每題請分別根據各篇文章之文意選出最適當的一個選項，標示在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。每題答對得2分，答錯不倒扣。

groups.passage:
Folk tales are stories passed down by word of mouth generation after generation. They often concern very strong or clever people who come from humble backgrounds. These people usually triumph over their enemies because of their wit and their great energy. Folk tales are both down-to-earth and highly imaginative.
Many folk tales originally had some basis in fact and grew out of the lives of real people. They changed, however, as they were told and retold. A man might once have fought a bear, for example, and the tales told about him might make him into the greatest bear fighter who ever lived. Through the power of imagination, folk tales can turn humble people into heroes. Many folk tales are also tall tales—stories of unbelievable events told with perfect seriousness. A tall tale, in other words, is a story in which the truth has been exaggerated.
A culture’s folk tales, fables, songs, and proverbs are an important part of its literature. By reading and listening to folk tales, we may gain a better understanding of the true values, beliefs, and goals of a people.

groups.passage:
It used to be that athletes and VIPs gave away their signatures for free, and a signed baseball or photograph would just sit on a shelf and collect dust. But nowadays, autographs (signatures) are big business.
Many athletes and VIPs demand payment for their signatures, and many people are willing to pay. Autograph dealers can be found in almost any sizable city, and collectors may get hundreds, even thousands, of dollars for things signed by anyone from Mozart to Madonna, Thomas Jefferson to JFK.
A 54-page manuscript written by Albert Einstein recently was sold for $398,500 at Christie’s in New York. And in 1994, Microsoft CEO (chief executive officer) Bill Gates paid $30.8 million for a handwritten notebook penned by Leonardo da Vinci. Meanwhile, fans across the U.S. are flocking to sports shows to have their heroes sign anything from a bat to a box of cereal.
What is the real reason many collectors want autographs? To connect with someone famous, or maybe even to imagine themselves as the hero they admire.

groups.passage: In Taiwan much time and energy are spent on getting a proper education and finding a good job. As a result, health concerns have been neglected. A new study by the Department of Health in Taiwan shows that more than half of the adult population in Taiwan lacks an understanding of important health problems. More than 2,000 adults took part in the survey to find out about their knowledge of diet, healthcare, disease control, and medication. Surprisingly, only 51 percent of the people surveyed understand that the common cold has no cure. Colds are caused by viruses, not bacteria, so taking medicine is absolutely no use at all. The problem is made worse by doctors who give their patients large doses of useless drugs. More than two-thirds believe that it is only the nicotine in cigarettes rather than the other chemicals that cause cancer. These people believe that if they smoke “light” cigarettes with less nicotine, they will not get cancer. Since 26 percent of Taiwanese adults smoke, such a misunderstanding will lead to more illness, suffering, and early death. But the outlook for health education in Taiwan is not all negative. The survey concludes that younger Taiwanese have a better understanding of health concerns than their parents, while senior citizens have the least understanding among the three age groups.

groups.passage:
“I have a regular film camera but I just don’t use it much,” said Ms. Lowery, 23, a computer programmer. “When I got married last year, I had all these pictures that didn’t come out right. With digital cameras, you aren’t spending money on film for wasted pictures,” she said.
And there are plenty of models from which to choose: from simple $200 point-and-shoot snappers to $1,000 wonders with all the features that any advanced amateur could want. The wide selection is a sure sign that in many consumers’ minds, digital cameras have risen from mere gadgets to must-have items.
Digital cameras offer more than just the instant previewing of pictures on small color screens. They can store dozens, sometimes hundreds, of images that can be printed easily at home or sent by e-mail. Although there are extra costs involved in going digital—the cost of memory cards for storage and the special paper for printing—many buyers have been willing to make the switch.
Although about 90 percent of American households still use film cameras, digital cameras are capturing a growing share of the consumer market. And the number of digital-camera households, now at about 10 percent, is certain to grow, as manufacturers introduce more and more cameras whose quality is as good as film cameras. Soon, even professionals will use them.
Salesmen expect digital cameras to be popular gifts this holiday season. “They are very hot this year,” said Yossi Fogel at B & H Photo in New York. “The prices have come down and the quality has gone up. Who wants to travel with 30 rolls of film? With a large memory card to store pictures, you can shoot and shoot and never have to worry about changing a roll. How many times have you missed a picture because you failed to reload the film?”

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of the digital camera over the film camera?

options.A: The user has to spend additional money for it.
options.B: It comes in many models for the customer.
options.C: It saves money from unwanted pictures.
options.D: Its pictures can be sent by e-mail.

questions.stem: According to this passage, the American households using digital cameras will increase if __________.
Which of the following is NOT TRUE about film cameras?

options.A: Their pictures can be printed at a photo shop.
options.B: Their pictures can be enlarged as desired.
options.C: Their pictures can be seen before they are printed.
options.D: Their pictures can be stored for a long time.

questions.stem: According to this article, digital cameras nowadays are used mainly by __________.
With a digital camera, it is necessary to __________.

options.B: print pictures at a photo shop
options.D: spend more time in using it

sections.title: 一、簡答題(10%)
sections.instructions:
說明︰1.閱讀下面這篇文章，然後簡答下列問題。答案必須寫在「答案卷」上。
2.請依序作答，並標明題號。答案應簡明扼要，只寫重要詞彙(key words)，約二至三個英文單詞(words)。每題2分，共10分。注意：請勿抄下整句或整行，否則不予計分。

groups.passage: Do women really use language differently from men? Over the years, researchers have given different answers to this question. In the legends of some cultures, it is even claimed that men and women speak different languages. If this were true, how could boys communicate with their mothers? One research report shows men and women use much the same grammar and vocabulary in English, although each sex uses certain kinds of words and structures more frequently than the other. Most men use more swear words, while far more women use adjectives such as “super” and “lovely,” and exclamations such as “Goodness me!” and “Oh dear!” Women have been found to ask more questions, make more use of positive and encouraging “noises,” use a wider range of intonation patterns, and make greater use of the pronouns “you” and “we.” By contrast, men are much more likely to interrupt (about three times as often in some studies), to argue about what has been said, to ignore or respond poorly to what has been said, to introduce more new topics into the conversation, and to make more assertions.

sections.title: 二、英文作文(20%)
sections.instructions:
說明︰1.依提示在「答案卷」上寫一篇英文作文。
2.文長120個單詞(words)左右。

questions.label: 作文
questions.stem: 提示︰以“Growing up is a/an _____ experience”為題寫一篇英文作文，描述你成長的經驗是令人興奮的(exciting)，令人困惑的(confusing)，快樂的(happy)或是痛苦的 (painful)。除了這些形容詞之外，你也可以用其他的形容詞來描述你成長的經驗。請務必提出具體的例子以描述你成長的經驗。(注意︰如果你用的形容詞以子音起始，請選擇冠詞“a”，如“a confusing experience”；如果你用的形容詞以母音起始，請選擇冠詞“an”，如“an exciting experience”。)

tags.topic: describe whether growing up has been an exciting, confusing, happy, painful (or otherwise described) experience for you, with concrete examples

extraction.method: Word 版（paper-4.doc → soffice 轉 docx → python-docx）為選文、句子配合題與中文說明的主要文字來源；詞彙題與閱讀題題幹的底線空格、作文提示的空格取自 pdftotext -layout 題本（paper-3.pdf）；兩者以程式逐字比對（去空白後全文比對，並以英文 token 序列核對所有選文、題幹、選項、選項庫皆在 PDF 文字中依序出現）；Read 看題本 PDF 全部 7 頁影像確認版面、題組、句子配合題表格與作文提示；封面 other-2.pdf 以 pdftotext 讀取考試時間；答案檔 answer-2.pdf 文字層為亂碼（Type 3 字型），以 Read 看第 1 頁影像並以 pdftoppm 200 dpi 放大裁切英文欄逐題抄錄 1–55 題；人工校對與標註。；查證者（verifier）獨立重做：pdftoppm 250 dpi 重新算圖 answer-2.pdf 並放大英文欄，逐題比對 1–55 題答案；Read 看題本 paper-3.pdf 全部 7 頁與封面影像；以程式將所有選文、題幹、選項、選項庫、說明、作文提示與 pdftotext 題本（去除頁首頁尾、空白正規化）逐字比對（選文全文逐字相同、字數一致），並與 soffice 轉出的 Word 版文字交叉比對；核對 stats-1/2.pdf 屬正式考；檢查標註。
issues: 結構核對：與 gsat-spec.json legacy_gsat「91–92」期別完全一致（spec 的 scope_note 註明只依正式考試核對、不含補考）——詞彙與慣用語 1–15（15分）、句子配合題 16–20（5分，右欄選項 A–J）、綜合測驗 21–30（10分，1篇×10空格）、文意選填 31–40（10分，選項 A–J）、閱讀測驗 41–55（4篇 3+3+4+5 題，每題2分，30分）、簡答題 5題×2分（10分，只寫重要詞彙 key words，約二至三個英文單詞）、英文作文 20分（文長「120個單詞(words)左右」，與 essay_length_by_year「91-94,96-98」相符）；合計 100 分。part 取自題本內頁「第壹部份：單一選擇題」「第貳部份：非選擇題」（內頁與封面 PDF 皆寫「部份」，Word 版封面寫「部分」），比照 gsat-91／92 填「單一選擇題」「非選擇題」。title 的「（補考）」比照 gsat-92-makeup 用全形括號（封面為全形「（補考）」）。

time_minutes：gsat-spec.json 把 90、91 學年度列為「題本未印考試時間（未驗證）」，但本卷封面（other-2.pdf，Word 版 paper-4.doc 開頭亦同）印有「考試時間：100 分鐘」「第壹部份 ˙單一選擇題共55 題」「第貳部份 ˙非選擇題共2大題」「選擇題答錯不倒扣」，故 time_minutes 填 100。題本內頁（paper-3.pdf 第1–7頁）本身沒有印考試時間。

答案：answer-2.pdf 為「九十一學年度學科能力測驗(補考)國文、英文及數學考科選擇題(含數學科填充題)答案」（第2頁為社會、自然，未使用），文字層是亂碼，以頁面影像（200 dpi 放大裁切英文欄）逐題抄錄英文 1–55 題：BDACDDACAB CABDC HGEBF BABCABDACD IGCDABHFEJ DACBDACBAB ADCBC；並逐題與題意核對無矛盾（例如 14 into doing、16 H discipline and a good plan、27 offering、37 aboard、40 off）。

評分原則與統計：units.json 中本卷只有 paper／paper_word／answer／other，沒有 scoring 與 stats。簡答題 1–5 的 answer／accepted_answers／scoring_notes 一律填 null（官方未公布參考答案，未自行作答）；作文 answer、scoring_notes 亦為 null。data/raw/ceec/gsat/91/ 中的 stats-1.pdf、stats-2.pdf 屬於 91 學年度正式考試（報考人數 146,627；stats-2 第1題標星號答案為 D，與 gsat-91 正式考第1題答案 D 相同，本卷第1題答案為 B），不可用於補考，全部小題 stats 填 null。validator 的「整份考卷沒有任何統計資料」warning 由此而來，屬合理（大考中心未公布補考統計）。
非選擇題題號：簡答題題本印為 1.–5.，與選擇題第1–5題重號；比照 gsat-91／92／92-makeup 慣例，no 保留 1–5、label 改為「簡答1」–「簡答5」；英文作文題本未編號，no 填 1、label 為「作文」。validator 的「題號重複 [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]」warning 由此而來，屬合理。

文字來源比對：Word 版與 pdftotext 題本去空白後逐字比對，英文內容完全一致，差異只有：(1) Word 版空格為帶底線的空白（詞彙、閱讀題幹、作文提示），改用 PDF 的底線字元；(2) 句子配合題說明第2點，PDF（頁面影像確認）為「標示在「答案卡」之「選擇題答案區」」，Word 版為「標示在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」」，依印製題本採 PDF 寫法；(3) Word 版第53題選項 (A) 漏印代號「(A)」，PDF 有；(4) pdftotext 把簡答題說明的「注意」「抄下」誤轉為「㊟意」「抄㆘」（字型對應問題），依頁面影像與 Word 版寫「注意：請勿抄下整句或整行，否則不予計分。」。文意選填說明「提供的 (A) 到 (J) 選項」照 Word 版與既有檔案保留空白（PDF 排版無明顯空白，屬版面差異）。說明文字的冒號照原文：一、二、三、五大題、簡答題、作文說明與「提示︰」「(注意︰」為 U+FE30「︰」，文意選填說明與簡答題「注意：」為全形「：」。

空白與格式正規化：排版造成的 Tab、連續空白與手動換行壓成單一空白；Word 版把綜合測驗第一段與 tip 1 拆成兩個段落（手動換行），已接回。綜合測驗選文的三條 tips 在題本為縮排編號清單，passage 中以換行分隔並保留「1. 」「2. 」「3. 」編號。詞彙題空格照 PDF 為 8 個底線；閱讀題幹空格照 PDF 為 9 個（41、43、46、47、49、50）或 10 個底線（44、45、52、54、55）；作文提示「a/an _____ experience」為 5 個底線（PDF）。克漏字空格原文「___(21)___」、文意選填「__31__」一律轉為 [[題號]]。各題組前「41-43 為題組」等標示為版面標題，未放入 passage。全卷英文在題本皆為粗體，NOT TRUE、NOT、TRUE 為原文大寫，無底線字、無圖表。

句子配合題照原文保留：左欄題幹去掉題號；右欄選項去掉代號字母以及緊接其後的「.」，保留開頭的「…」（比照 gsat-90／91）。原卷右欄格式不一（PDF 與 Word 版相同）：A–F 為「A.…」，G、H 為「G…」「H…」（代號後無句點），I 為「I…. keep in mind the direction of the street.」（省略號之後才是句點，應為「I.…」的排版錯誤），options_bank.I 比照 gsat-91 照原文寫作「…. keep in mind the direction of the street.」；J 為「J.… better than studying alone at home.」，省略號後有空格，照錄為「… better than studying alone at home.」。
